entities.name: Gaius Coelius Caldus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Coelius Caldus was a Roman consul who played a pivotal role in shaping the Late Republic's politics during the tumultuous period of 146–49 BCE. His involvement with Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus underscores the complex web of alliances and rivalries within the Roman elite.

Caldus's actions helped to exacerbate the instability that ultimately led to the downfall of the Roman Republic, transforming it into the Roman Empire under Augustus Caesar.

The legacy of Gaius Coelius Caldus can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, which ruled Rome from 27 BCE to 68 CE. His influence also contributed to the increased power and control of the Roman Senate, setting the stage for the imperial system that would dominate Western politics for centuries.

In the annals of history, Gaius Coelius Caldus stands as a testament to the enduring power of ambition and the fickle nature of political alliances in ancient Rome.
